reply.text:
Scratch files confirmed removed (no `_smoke*` in the earlier find output was needed — the `rm -f` already ran cleanly).

## Summary

Built the Customers page at the app root, following the existing module architecture:

- **`services/customers.contract.ts`** — the `Customer` type and `CustomerApi` interface (`list(signal)`).
- **`services/customers.http.ts`** — real adapter, `fetch('/api/customers')`, surfacing the server's `{ error }` message on failure.
- **`services/customers.context.ts`** — `useCustomerApi()`, same pattern as `devices.context.ts`.
- **`modules/customers/`** — `customers.queries.ts` (`useCustomers()`, `retry: false` so the button-driven retry is the only retry path), `Customers.tsx` (loading/error/table, exactly one visible via early returns), `customers.css`, `index.ts`.
- **`main.tsx`** — now mounts `<Customers />` wired to the HTTP adapter instead of the devices demo.
- **`styles/global.css`** — added the module's stylesheet import.

Verified: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm test` all pass. Since no browser automation tool was available in this sandbox, I verified actual behavior with a throwaway happy-dom harness (same technique this repo's own tests use) driving the real `useCustomers` hook against the live server at `127.0.0.1:57162`: confirmed pending → success with real customer rows, and a separate run confirmed a failed request surfaces as an error after exactly one attempt (no silent auto-retry) and `refetch()` recovers — matching the loading/error/retry requirements. The scratch scripts were deleted afterward.
